positive.prompt: I'm about to dispatch this implementation task to a subagent — how should I write the spawn prompt so it does not need re-work?
Write the task cards for this milestone before I hand them off to implementation agents
My subagents keep returning work that fails verification and I keep re-spawning them, and token spend on bulk implementation is climbing

negative.prompt: Write a failing test for the date parser before I implement it

evals.prompt: I need to hand an implementation task to a Sonnet subagent. Set up the delegation so it produces committable work without re-briefing.
evals.expected_output: A card-based spawn contract: model tier, cited rules, env-facts, evidence-based acceptance, and an orchestrator-side spot-check plan
expectations: Work is placed on the appropriate model tier rather than kept on the top model by default
A task card carries the goal, cited rules, steps, and evidence-based acceptance instead of an ad-hoc prompt
Acceptance names an exact command and observable, and synthetic substitutes are forbidden
The orchestrator spot-checks evidence rather than re-running full gates on unchanged code
